title: Drafting Sleeve Cap Curve – Keeping Curved Segment Length Constant When Moving Curve Points
content:
I want to draft a sleeve cap curve.

![7b27c04208964f82b99e0fe6b2d4137b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/c139159010084bfa98a072c30e2dd9df/images/7b27c04208964f82b99e0fe6b2d4137bScreenshot%202026-05-21%20at%2014.55.02.png)

The distance between point A and point B is 18.52 (It is surely the Back Armscye measure), and this length must remain constant.

However, I want to shape this straight segment into a sleeve cap curve while keeping the total curve length unchanged.

Is there a method for this?

For example:

If I add a curve point and use drag & drop to form a curve, one area becomes more convex. But ideally, CLO should automatically adjust the rest of the curve so that the overall curve length remains fixed at 18.52.

Is there any workflow, tool, or constraint in CLO that allows this kind of controlled curve deformation while preserving segment length?

Or do you have any recommended approach for drafting sleeve cap curves under this constraint?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: If you get me right This is definitely a CLO question.I didn't ask you how to draw a sleeve cap curve physically or theory (at Pattern Drafting Domain) behind It or results (If It will fit or not.)What I ask you If I can fix the measure while modifying the straight line. I thought maybe CLO compensate the line length change while I modifying. (So It fixes the measure.) When I go in x direction in some area on the line CLO automatically go flatten or make changes some areas in the way that the measure does NOT change.While drawing It on the paper I revise the sleeve cap curve by erasing by an eraser and and redraw the part of the line and re-check the sleeve cap. Let's say 2-3 times. check and revise.So I do It like this on CLO? Modify then check the measure and modify again.Or Can CLO fix the length by compensating my modifications on the curve.???
Reply 1: Hi There. As Ariel already said, No You cannot fix a length of a straight line and then curve it. This is just real life. A straight line is the shortest form of a line, any added shaping or curve will naturally change the length(longer). That is just real world geometry. In drafting a sleeve the shape usually starts as the triangle as you have in your image, but those sides are not the finished lengths. After those are drawn curve tools are used to shape the cap . And those lengths will be longer than the sides of the triangle.Now as Ariel has already mentioned, if you know the length you wants a Segment to be you can always just use the Change Length feature to shorted or length to a specified amount. https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/c139159010084bfa98a072c30e2dd9df
Reply 2: Understood. Thank you very much.

Comment 2: This is a pattern making question and NOT a CLO question. In pattern books you draw this to start and then change the shape, and the length will change. Most of this question should be posted to a pattern making forum and not here for more in depth pattern making answers. If you know the length You can always curve the line and then after use the Change length feature in 2D after and adjust the length to the exact amount.
content_description: This page aims to explore methods and workflows in CLO for drafting a sleeve cap curve that maintains a fixed total curve length while allowing controlled shape adjustments.

title: DXF vs PACX File?
content:
DXF vs PACX File?

What is the difference between 2 export methods in the 3D State?

A) File - Export - DXF

B) File - Save As - Pattern (.pacx File)

What are the difference between those DXF and Pacx files?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Is there a data difference between them? (Like Arrangement info, Sewing Info etc.)

Comment 2: Is all the data contained the same?

Comment 3: A PACX file is a 2D pattern file that can only be opened in the CLO program.A DXF file can be opened and viewed in various 2D apparel CAD programs.
